newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Princess Diana said caught in spy video.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Princess Diana said caught in spy video.

text.p: A "spy video" apparently showing Princess Diana frolicking in sports pants and bra with her lover James Hewitt was shown on British television on Tuesday in the latest scandal to rock the royal family.

The tabloid Sun, which broke news of the grainy 80-second film, said on Tuesday it confirmed Diana's fears that she had been under secret surveillance during the break-up of her 15-year marriage to heir to the throne Prince Charles.
Buckingham Palace denied the black-and-white video, confirmed as genuine by Hewitt, was used as a bargaining chip in her divorce with Charles, finalised in August.

Sky Television broadcast the video, which appeared to show Diana stripping down to cycling pants and sports bra, kissing Hewitt, riding on his back and playfully pillow-fighting. It was shot from outside through a window into a bedroom.
"I do not believe it is a hoax, otherwise we would not be printing it," Sun editor Stuart Higgins said.
Diana has admitted adultery with Hewitt and, in a sensational television interview in November, said she had "adored" him during their five-year affair.
Diana has in the past claimed that her telephone calls were bugged. Transcripts of alleged calls she made to male friends have been printed in British newspapers.
The Sun said the fact the film was black and white indicated it had been taken by a professional outfit. It was apparently taken at the Highgrove country home of Charles and Diana.
A Conservative member of parliament, Harry Greenaway, said he planned to raise the question of whether Diana was spied on by British agents with the government.

"Without in any way judging the princess's life, which is private, there ought to be an inquiry into how this happened and who authorised it," Greenaway said. Despite the furore surrounding the video, Diana looked relaxed and smiled broadly as she launched a fund for a support centre run by a leading British AIDS charity. Diana has been a strong supporter of those involved in the fight against AIDS. Hewitt, a cavalry officer who served in the Gulf War, was condemned as a cad and a bounder by fellow officers in 1994 when journalist Anna Pasternak published "Princess in Love," a romantic "faction" account of Hewitt's affair with the princess.
Hewitt told the tabloid: "I am convinced there were illicit spying operations -- undoubtedly, undoubtedly."
"I heard about some tapes and some films of us together and one theory was that the princess's divorce settlement was only half what she wanted because of this sort of material," he said.
But Buckingham Palace denied any involvement in the video.

"The princess admitted an affair with James Hewitt when she appeared on (the BBC TV documentary) Panorama before the divorce negotiations. So how could this video have been used against her," a palace spokesman said.
The revelations were another blow to Queen Elizabeth, already facing a crisis over the debts and love life of her other troublesome former daughter-in-law, the Duchess of York.

In her Panorama interview, Diana suggested she had been under surveillance and efforts were made to discredit her after alleged tapes of her conversations with a male friend were released to a newspaper.

In October 1994, a former Royal Marine commando was interviewed by Special Branch security officers over claims he made in a tabloid newspaper that he led a military unit which kept watch on the lovers.
